name: Hashflow deprecated router RFQ-m caller-supplied pool
summary: The deprecated HashflowRouter's cross-chain RFQ-m trade (0x0031b016) pulled the quoted amount from quote.trader to a caller-supplied quote.pool and left the authorization check to that pool. Attackers named their own contract as the pool, answered the check with true, and drained wallets still approving the router on Polygon, Ethereum, Arbitrum, BNB Chain and Avalanche from June 2023 on.
notes: Anchor: MEV bot 0x31487bbd8c2e79465940cc07dec049dc0845331b replayed the drain through its own contract 0xb6d3c5d1 on Polygon 113 s before the first Ethereum copycat (eip155:1:0xf2fbfe88…) and bridged the proceeds out via Multichain. Earlier drains from 2023-06-14 by 0xbdf38b7475ff810325aa39e988fb80e0aa007e84 (refs) ran through its OhNo contracts, which credit each pulled balance to its victim for recover(); the white hat sent leftovers to 2-of-n Safe 0x7eb7bb6325df1393b91ff30e1bee2f05b8799f6b, which returned 36,888.58 USDC to a victim drained in eip155:1:0xdedda493…; they are an affiliated rescue (rule 5), excluded from anchor, campaign and loss.

Only the Polygon router is a target, as the anchor executed only it; the Ethereum (0x79cdfd7b…), Arbitrum (0x36c543b8…), BNB Chain (0x375e05f6…) and Avalanche (0x43b4bf87…) routers are same-code (0xd9d407dd…) deployments by 0xe8bc44ae4ba6eddb88c8c087fd9b479dff729850 in April 2022, exploited in the same campaign (rule 4). The exploit reads no router storage, so the deployment is the reset.

Campaign: Ethereum from a full trace_filter scan of the router; the other chains from every address that ever approved the router, tracing its token transfers in transactions it did not send (Polygon and BNB Chain from June 2023; sampled earlier Polygon traffic used only the live 0x1e9a2e92 trade, ending May 2022). Listed are the first transaction per chain and those pulling at least 10,000 USD-stablecoin units; three 2026 BNB Chain dust pulls via 0x1e9a2e92 are not counted.

Loss is the decoded quote amounts pulled from traders, valued with loss.mjs on Ethereum and Avalanche and with DefiLlama daily prices (CoinGecko twins for bridged stablecoins, WETH, WPOL, WBNB and CAKE lacking history) on the other chains, where loss.mjs's per-transaction pricing could not finish 2,000 transactions; on Avalanche the two methods differ by 0.08%. Arbitrum wallet 0x6a04941de896e4215eeb8e6eb1b72ad2904d2402, which approved the router in 2022 and was dormant from November 2022, lost 510,100 USDT to drainer 0x342d66fa (sold for ETH by 0x0d7a0f89) and 227,460 USDT to 0x90ac7a74; it is an ordinary victim. Unpriced pool receipt tokens (ZCP-USDC, ZCP-USDT, LP-TSC-USDC/USDT, about 15,900 units) are omitted.
